thread:
anton: Ran a focused nsys on the TRT+vLLM integration (8x batching, seq=1024). Seeing unexpected time in the wrapper/scheduler path, not just in the engine. Posting top-line and a couple notes.

sara: dropped a signal, please paste the nsys summary (or upload the .qdrep). :mag:

anton: summary paste below (trimmed). key bits first: lots of `cudaLaunchKernel` overhead, big chunk in cuBLASLt, and nontrivial CPU-side wait in the vLLM scheduler.

```
nsys summary (trimmed):
Total GPU activities: 183.2 ms
  cuBLASLt::Gemm      92.4 ms   (50.4%)
  TRT::execute        47.1 ms   (25.7%)
  cudaLaunchKernel    23.8 ms   (13.0%)
  cudaMemcpy HtoD     9.7 ms    (5.3%)
  cudaMemcpy DtoH     6.2 ms    (3.4%)
CPU activities (host):
  vLLM scheduler overhead (Python->C) 41 ms
  wrapper marshalling / arg copy     18 ms
Notes: kernel times include small custom kernels + cuBLAS calls invoked inside TRT engines; cudaLaunchKernel represents repeated launches from the wrapper (not single fused graph).
```

nate: that's interesting — TRT::execute at 47ms but cuBLAS is 92ms. Means the engine triggers cuBLAS work that dominates. The `cudaLaunchKernel` number suggests we aren't using cudaGraph or persistent kernels; frequent launches add up.

anton: exactly. Also saw per-request KV copy spikes in a few traces: when cache miss+rebuild happens we memcpy ~1.2MB per token chunk H2D repeatedly. That shows up as the HtoD bursts.

sara: can you paste the short perfetto timeline snippet (just the CPU timeline around the scheduler + the corresponding GPU slices)?

anton: pasted minimal timeline snippet — CPU thread shows repeated `call_engine()` entries each ~2-6ms, while GPU shows a lot of short cuBLAS segments interleaved.

```
Perfetto snippet (simplified):
Host thread: | call_engine | call_engine | call_engine | ...  (each 3-5ms)
GPU timeline: | cuBLAS(20ms) | small-kernel(1ms) | cuBLAS(18ms) | memcpy(4ms) | ...
Correlation: many host `call_engine` calls overlap identical GPU work windows; host waits for stream syncs in some cases.
```

nate: preliminary hypothesis:
- vLLM wrapper makes repeated engine calls from Python -> C -> TRT (no batching of engine calls across requests inside the process)
- Each engine call launches cuBLAS kernels (heavy) and incurs `cudaLaunchKernel` overhead for each small kernel in the engine
- KV cache copy (HtoD/DtoH) happens at the wrapper boundary for some code paths, adding memcpy costs per request

sara: actionables?

anton: proposals:
- move engine invocation path off the Python request thread to a dedicated C++ dispatcher thread with a bounded queue (reduce Python dispatch jitter)
- experiment with cudaGraph capture of the TRT engine path (if model/shape stable) to collapse repeated kernel launches
- pin KV cache in GPU memory and avoid HtoD on hot prefix paths (use device pointers + zero-copy for small control metadata)
- add a microbench that isolates `TRT::execute` and the internal cuBLAS calls to confirm where time is spent (run with `CUBLAS_LOGINFO` and per-kernel counters)

perf-bot: created ticket ENG-4593 with summary "trt-vllm: wrapper/scheduler overhead + memcpy hotspots" and attached nsys qdrep.

sara: good list. I'll own the cudaGraph experiment (I'll try seq=1024 with batch 8 and 16; if shape variance kills graph reuse we'll fallback).

nate: I'll instrument wrapper to emit:
- per-call timestamps (pre/post native call)
- size of KV copy (bytes)
- whether call used pinned memory
Will push a patch to `perf/eng_runtime/trt_integration` and add a microbench harness.

anton: one more datapoint: I re-ran with `TRT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` toggled — latency dropped ~12% but the `cudaLaunchKernel` bulk remained for non-captured pieces. So graphs help but don't fully close the gap (and they require stricter shape stability).

sara: ok. prioritize pinned-memory + dispatcher thread first, then graphs. Also add a regression test in CI that runs a short nvprof/nsys on the hot path (smoke, not full).

anton: thanks — I'll attach the raw qdrep and a trimmed nvprof flame in the ticket. For the thread: ping me if you want the raw CUDA API traces (I have them). :thumbsup:

nate: +1. will instrument and report numbers by EOD tomorrow.
